Our gospel today reminds us that there’s no need to feel overwhelmed by all the evil that the media feed into our homes each day, almost giving us a sense that there’s nothing we can do. There are pl enty around us who need food and drink, for body and soul; there are plenty who need to be welcomed, to be clothed, to be visited. Why do we hesitate? Could it be that I didn’t recognize the King that evening in Paris ? It’s not by chance that this is the gospel passage that we read for the feast of Christ the King, as this is how the King chooses to be fed, clothed etc. – “youdid it to Me”. I don’t know who the young ladies were – I don’t know if they have ever been inside church, temple or synagogue. But if that’s their habitual outlook on life, they need have no worries. Such were my thoughts as I later tucked into a nice hot meal, in warm comfortable surroundings! Please return completed lists to reception, to our sacristan or to one of the priests. Youth 2000 Christmas Retreat: Calling all young people aged 16 –35! Join us at the Youth 2000 Christmas Retreat in Newbridge College, Co. Kildare, from 11th-13th December 2026. This is a donation-only event, with free buses available across the country and all meals included. Expect inspiring talks and workshops, Mass, music, prayer, and plenty of opportunities to chill out and meet other young Catholics. Whether you are new to the faith or looking to be refreshed, all are welcome . To register or find out more, visit youth2000.ie or follow @Youth2000Ireland.
